subject: How to get a shiny UI widget type at runtime

messages.author: 2442f866a919f44d
messages.subject: How to get a shiny UI widget type at runtime
parts: I was wondering whether there is a way to find out the widget type of a given input at runtime. Say i have something like input$maxAllowed implemented as a sliderInput in my ui.R and i want to get the 'sliderInput' type of the input (not just the fact that it is an integer value) in the server.R. I want to implement a 'save settings' functionality in my apps and want to keep the code as generic as possible - hence it would be great to be able to write a 'save settings' routine that can store the widget type along with the values and a load routine that can then update the UI elements based on the stored types & values. Any help would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: How to get a shiny UI widget type at runtime
parts:
I agree with Barbara, it sounds like what you want should be achievable with the bookmarking feature.

If you're really keen on getting the type of an input, you can see how shinyjs achieves that (it's needed in the shinyjs::reset() function because a different update function is called depending on the input type). It's not super straight forward code, but it is documented so if you spend half an hour looking into it you'll be able to use the same method in your own code. Relevant code: saving the type of each input using javascript: https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/inst/srcjs/shinyjs-default-funcs.js#L284-L392 and retrieving the input type in R https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/R/reset.R

There are of course other ways to achieve this, this is just an example you can try to follow
